points.response: The app reason the driver picked does not make it a no-show: NS-0 sends the case to NS-1 only if all NS-1 conditions hold, and here the arrival condition fails outright — he tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 while 613 m away (F6, F21) and was never within 200 m (F1), with driver_arrived_at null (F5).
NS-1(iii) requires at least 1 in-app message AND at least 1 phone call; the record shows 2 messages but 0 in-app calls (F4), so the contact prong fails however the messages read.

NS-1(ii) counts the free wait from the later of the scheduled pickup time and arrival, and there was no arrival: he signalled at 08:16:00 from 613 m out (F6) and spent 0 s inside the 200 m radius (F1, F22), so no waiting threshold was met at the pickup point.

Being stationary 08:13:10–08:19:30 at (1.2958, 103.8495) is not staying at the pickup point: that spot is 613 m from pickup (F2, F1), and NS-1(iv) requires presence at the pickup location, not merely a parked car elsewhere.

The rider's 08:14 and 08:17 messages show she was at the Victoria St entrance waiting (F9, F11); the failure to connect was the driver's 613 m standoff (F1, F2), and his only substantive reply at 08:19 was "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling" (F12).

The $5.00 figure matching the published no-show fee does not validate it: NS-2 voids the fee when any NS-1 condition fails, and all three fail here (location F1/F6/F5, wait F22, contact F4), so the $5.00 must be refunded (F7).

The profile cuts the other way on the add-on: the driver's own record shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F20) while the rider has 0 disputes and a 4.9 rating (F19), supporting the NS-2 flag for a falsely marked arrival.

Band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Victoria Street is ordinary slow traffic, not a closure or incident (F15, F17, F18), and the record's own signal JAM_CLAIM_UNSUPPORTED marks the jam excuse unsupported; in any event a traffic reason would not excuse a mismarked arrival under NS-1.
Conceded on the location point: GPS puts the closest approach at 612 m and never inside 200 m (F1), and no driver_arrived_at was recorded (F5), so NS-1(i) is not met on this record.

Conceded: the tap at 08:16:00 occurred at 613 m from the pickup with 0 s inside the 200 m radius (F6) and is flagged as ARRIVAL_LOCATION_MISMATCH (F21), so the arrival marker does not satisfy NS-1(i).

Conceded: the stationary record 08:13:10–08:19:30 places the driver 613 m from the pickup (F2), which is not "at the pick-up location" for the purpose of NS-1(iv); this is the weakest link in my client's case and I do not dispute it.

Conceded on the contact pair: F4 shows 2 in-app messages but 0 in-app calls, and NS-1(iii) requires at least one message AND at least one call, so this condition fails as written; my client's two messages (F10, F12) are contact attempts but cannot substitute for the call the clause requires.

Partially conceded: I accept that the "waited more than 3 minutes" claim (F12) is contradicted by 0 min 0 s within 200 m (F1, F22), but the driver did remain stationary for 6 min 20 s (F2) — the failure is that he waited in the wrong place, not that he left the rider standing while driving off.

I do not concede the traffic point in full: my client said the street was jammed (F14) and the LTA record does show Victoria Street at 20–29 km/h, band 3 (F15) — slow-moving, though not the incident-or-band-1/2 congestion NS-1/RD-4 treats as justification; F16 and F17 rightly defeat any claim of closure or incident, and F23 rightly flags the exaggeration.

Conceded that the rider's messages (F9 at 08:14, F11 at 08:17) show she was present and trying to connect, while the driver's closest approach stayed at 612 m (F1); my client's F10 "I'm here already" was not accurate against the GPS record.

I do not contest that on the record as it stands at least NS-1(i) fails, so the $5.00 fee is voided under NS-2 and the money goes back to the rider; what I ask is that this not be decided as a pure fraud case, because the one thing the record does establish is that my client remained stationary for 6 min 20 s attempting the trip (F2, F4) rather than taking the fee and driving away — the facts the rider relies on are GPS facts (F1, F6, F21, F22), and the profile is not available to carry the flag_account add-on by itself under TH-3.

The driver's two prior upheld no-show disputes are no-show matters only (route: 0, no-show: 2, F20), and NS-9 is the rider-repeat clause, not a driver clause; RD-6 applies only to route deviations and this case has no off-route segment, so neither clause supports an account flag here, and the profile never decides the current case.

Withdrawn as a finding on the merits: the app reason rider_no_show (F3) does not survive the GPS record (F1, F5), because NS-0 routes the case by the conditions in NS-1, and those conditions are not met.
Withdrawn: I accept that a wait counted from a tap made 613 m from the pickup (F6) cannot satisfy NS-1(ii), because the wait must run from a valid arrival (NS-1(i)).

Standing, but with less force than I first gave it: F9 and F11 genuinely show the rider was at the entrance while my client was 613 m away (F1, F2), which shows she was not trying to avoid the ride, but it also shows the two of them were never in a position to meet; I rely on it only to show my client did not abandon a rider who had gone silent.

Revised: I no longer put the traffic point as a justification, only as an explanation of the driver's message — Victoria Street was slow at band 3, 20–29 km/h (F15), but no incident was logged (F17), so the "jammed solid" wording (F14) overstates a 20–29 km/h road and I do not rely on it to defeat the rider's claim.
